payload.task_text:
The product team wants to analyze customer review quality across product categories to prioritize product improvement efforts. Query WooCommerce product review data and link it to product categories to understand how different categories perform with customers.

Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Category Analysis" with columns: Category, Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating (rounded to 2 decimal places), Five_Star_Count, and Five_Star_Rate (the percentage of reviews that are 5 stars, rounded to 1 decimal). Sort by Category alphabetically. The second sheet should be called "Top Products" and list the top 10 highest-rated products that have at least 3 reviews, with columns: Product_Name (truncated to 50 characters if needed), Category, Review_Count, and Avg_Rating (rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort by Avg_Rating descending, then Review_Count descending.

Create a Notion database called "Product Review Insights" with properties for Category (title), Product_Count (number), Review_Count (number), Avg_Rating (number), and Five_Star_Rate (number). Populate it with one entry per category from the Category Analysis sheet.

Email the analysis to product_team@store.com with subject "Product Review Analysis Report" and include a summary of which categories have the highest and lowest ratings in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two genuine dependency waves with exactly three sub-agents total. The first agent computes the complete store join once; the two artifact writers then run in parallel from one canonical category table.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Explore sub-agent:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Use one Explore sub-agent to retrieve the complete product and review endpoints read-only using `perPage=100` and increasing pages until each has a short or empty terminal page. Omit the optional review `status` argument, preserve every observed status, and filter only as the original task requires. Join strictly by Product_ID; a product contributes to each observed category exactly according to its source categories. Compute the compact per-category Product_Count, Review_Count, rating sum/average, Five_Star_Count/Rate, and the eligible products with at least three reviews. Rank Top Products by average rating descending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID. Return the full compact category and top-ten tables directly, plus endpoint page/row/status controls, join/category coverage, and duplicate/tie checks. Do not modify the store or create deliverables.

After Wave 1, the main agent independently checks the counts, rates, rankings, and tie order, then freezes one immutable category/top-product handoff for both writers.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 Coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole writer of `Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx`. Create the exact two sheets once from the frozen tables, with exact headers, truncation, sorting, row limits, rounding, and literal values. Read both sheets back and return the path plus complete row/value controls.

   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole owner of the exact-title `Product Review Insights` database. Search exact title once first and reuse an exact match, otherwise create the database once with the exact property types; then create exactly one page per frozen category, sending each page in a SINGLE create call that carries all its properties together — never update properties one at a time, never re-read pages between inserts, and do not verify row-by-row. When all rows are inserted, issue ONE final database query to confirm the row count, and return the database ID, property names and final row count. Do not write the workbook.

   3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole owner of the summary email to product_team@store.com with the exact task subject: body built ONLY from the frozen tables — the total product/review counts, the highest-rated and lowest-rated categories with their average ratings and five-star rates, and the complete per-category breakdown. Paginate Sent search and match the exact recipient/subject before an at-most-once send, then read the retained message back and return its ID. Do not write the workbook or database.

After all three writers return, reconcile every category across source, workbook, database and the sent message against the same frozen tables. Read back all three outputs. Repairs belong only to the original writer, and there is no separate validation wave.

After the final wave completes, do not invoke the agent-dispatch tool again — not even an empty or exploratory dispatch attempt (a dispatch that returns zero agents is wasted work). Any remaining checks, emails or small writes are main-agent direct work completed in one pass.

nodes.text:
You are a planning sub-agent. Decompose the following task into an ordered list of subtasks. Do NOT execute the task — only produce a plan. You may use read-only tools to inspect the environment if needed (e.g., listing files in the workspace, checking WooCommerce product/review/category counts, checking Notion/email connection status), but do not create/modify anything.

TASK (given by user):
The product team wants to analyze customer review quality across product categories to prioritize product improvement efforts. Query WooCommerce product review data and link it to product categories to understand how different categories perform with customers.

1. Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx with two sheets:
   - Sheet 1 "Category Analysis": columns Category, Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating (rounded to 2 decimal places), Five_Star_Count, Five_Star_Rate (percentage of reviews that are 5 stars, rounded to 1 decimal). Sort by Category alphabetically.
   - Sheet 2 "Top Products": top 10 highest-rated products that have at least 3 reviews, columns Product_Name (truncated to 50 chars if needed), Category, Review_Count, Avg_Rating (rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort by Avg_Rating descending, then Review_Count descending.

2. Create a Notion database called "Product Review Insights" with properties: Category (title), Product_Count (number), Review_Count (number), Avg_Rating (number), Five_Star_Rate (number). Populate it with one entry per category from the Category Analysis sheet.

3. Email the analysis to product_team@store.com with subject "Product Review Analysis Report", including a summary of which categories have the highest and lowest ratings in the email body.

ENVIRONMENT CONTEXT:
- Workspace (where the Excel file must be written): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-excel-notion/workspace
- Available tools: WooCommerce MCP (products list/get, products reviews list, product categories list), Excel MCP (create workbook, write data, etc.), Notion MCP (create database, create page, query), Email MCP (send_email), filesystem MCP, local python execution.
- WooCommerce review data: product reviews can be fetched via mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_reviews_list (optionally filtered by productId). Products via mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list (paginated, perPage up to 100). Categories via mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_categories_list. Note: product category names may need to be resolved from product objects (categories array) or from the product itself.

PLAN REQUIREMENTS — for each subtask specify:
- dispatch decision: `self` (main agent), `explore`, or `coder`
- whether the subtask is independent (parallelizable) or must wait for another subtask's output (dependency)
- concrete acceptance criteria / deliverable

Consider in your plan:
- How to enumerate all products (pagination) and their categories (products may have multiple categories — decide a rule, e.g., use primary/first category).
- How to enumerate all reviews per product (pagination), compute per-category aggregates (product count = number of products in category, review count = total reviews, avg rating, five-star count, five-star rate).
- How to compute per-product aggregates for the Top Products sheet (only products with >= 3 reviews, top 10 by avg rating desc then review count desc, name truncated to 50 chars).
- Data consistency: the Notion database entries and the email must be derived from the same computed numbers.
- Ordering: Excel creation, Notion creation, email sending are independent once data is computed — but Notion needs a database to exist before pages are added; email needs the summary.

Return the ordered subtask list with dependencies and dispatch decisions, plus any risks (e.g., pagination limits, missing reviews, products with no category).
Plan product review analysis task

You are a coder sub-agent working on a WooCommerce product review analysis. Produce a canonical dataset (JSON) and an Excel workbook. Use ONLY the granted MCP tools (filesystem, woocommerce, excel, local python). Do NOT touch Notion or email — another agent handles those.

WORKSPACE (write outputs here):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-excel-notion/workspace

STEP 1 — LOAD PRODUCTS:
Read the file that contains the FULL WooCommerce products list (97 products, JSON array):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-excel-notion/workspace/.tool_results/mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list-call_01_qA5mOJlIZLHWpoZCKCLH8575-feaba240-66b3-45bb-ad7f-753d26bad48f.txt
Use mcp__filesystem__read_text_file (or python) to read it, then parse the JSON array. For each product keep: `id`, `name`, and the category name of the FIRST entry of its `categories` array (products have exactly one category in practice; if `categories` is empty, assign "Uncategorized"). IMPORTANT: map categories by NAME as it appears in the product object (e.g. "TV & Home Theater", "Audio", "Cameras", "Electronics", "Headphones", "Home Appliances", "Speakers", "Watches") — do NOT rely on category numeric ids, they are inconsistent between the products payload and the category list.

STEP 2 — LOAD REVIEWS:
Fetch ALL approved product reviews via mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_reviews_list with perPage=100 and status="approved", iterating page=1, 2, 3, ... until an empty page is returned. There are 396 approved reviews total (review ids 1..396; pages 1-4 have data, page 5+ are empty — verify by paginating until empty). For each review keep `product_id` and `rating`. Ignore non-approved reviews (the status filter handles this).

STEP 3 — COMPUTE (single source of truth):
Write a Python script (via mcp__local__python_execute) that:
a) Per CATEGORY: for each category present among products, compute:
   - Product_Count = number of distinct products in that category
   - Review_Count = total number of approved reviews belonging to products in that category
   - Avg_Rating = mean of all ratings in the category, rounded to 2 decimal places
   - Five_Star_Count = number of reviews with rating == 5
   - Five_Star_Rate = (Five_Star_Count / Review_Count * 100) rounded to 1 decimal place; if Review_Count == 0, use 0.0
   Sort rows by Category alphabetically (A→Z).
b) Per PRODUCT: compute Review_Count and Avg_Rating (mean rounded to 2 dp) from the actual reviews. Keep only products with Review_Count >= 3. Sort by Avg_Rating descending, then Review_Count descending, and take the top 10. For each: Product_Name truncated to exactly 50 characters if longer (plain slice name[:50], NO ellipsis), Category (the product's category name), Review_Count, Avg_Rating (rounded 2 dp).
c) Persist EVERYTHING to /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-excel-notion/workspace/analysis_data.json with keys: "category_analysis" (list of dicts with Category, Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating, Five_Star_Count, Five_Star_Rate), "top_products" (list of dicts with Product_Name, Category, Review_Count, Avg_Rating), "email_summary" (text describing which category has the highest Avg_Rating and which has the lowest Avg_Rating, with their Avg_Rating values; tie-break by Review_Count if needed). Also keep raw (unrounded) values if useful.

STEP 4 — BUILD EXCEL:
Create /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-excel-notion/workspace/Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx using the Excel MCP tools:
- mcp__excel__create_workbook(filepath=...)
- Inspect what default sheet(s) exist with mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata; then create/rename worksheets so the workbook contains EXACTLY two sheets:
  Sheet 1 named "Category Analysis" with header row: Category, Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating, Five_Star_Count, Five_Star_Rate — followed by the category rows sorted alphabetically (same data as analysis_data.json).
  Sheet 2 named "Top Products" with header row: Product_Name, Category, Review_Count, Avg_Rating — followed by the top 10 rows (same data as analysis_data.json).
- Use mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel to write the data (list of lists: header + rows). Write Avg_Rating and Five_Star_Rate as NUMERIC values with the specified rounding (e.g. 4.63, 61.5) — not strings. Delete any leftover default sheet (e.g. "Sheet1") with mcp__excel__delete_worksheet.
- Verify by reading back with mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel for both sheets and confirm headers, row counts, sorts, and rounding.

RETURN IN YOUR FINAL MESSAGE (verbatim, complete):
1. The full category_analysis table (all rows, all 6 fields).
2. The full top_products table (all 10 rows).
3. The email_summary text you generated.
4. Confirmation that analysis_data.json and Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx exist in the workspace, with the exact sheet names and row counts.
Do not summarize or abbreviate the tables — the caller needs the exact values.
Compute aggregates and build Excel

You are working on a WooCommerce product review analysis task. Your job is to produce a CANONICAL, COMPLETE dataset and an Excel file. Prior work in this workspace is CONTAMINATED (a previous agent saved truncated/incomplete JSON files, e.g. products_data.json only has a single 'category' field per product and is missing the Headphones and Speakers categories). DO NOT read or trust any existing files in the workspace, especially anything under .tool_results/ — always pull fresh data from the WooCommerce API using the mcp__woocommerce__* tools.

Workspace root: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-excel-notion/workspace

STEP 1 — Pull complete product catalog:
Use mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=15 and page=1..6 (there are exactly 82 products, ids 1..82; page1=ids 82..68, page2=67..53, page3=52..38, page4=37..23, page5=22..8, page6=7..1). Keep pulling pages until a page returns fewer than 15 items. For EVERY product you MUST capture: id, name, and the FULL categories array (each category has id + name). Do NOT use perPage=100 (output may be truncated).

IMPORTANT: In the WooCommerce product payloads, category IDs do NOT match the product-category-list IDs — you MUST match categories by NAME, never by ID. The 8 canonical category names are: Audio, Cameras, Electronics, Headphones, Home Appliances, Speakers, TV & Home Theater, Watches.

STEP 2 — Pull all approved reviews:
Use mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_reviews_list with status="approved", perPage=100, page=1..4 until a page returns fewer than 100 items (total is 396 reviews, ids 396..1). For every review capture: id, product_id, rating (1-5). Verify each page returns a full JSON array; if any page looks truncated, retry with a smaller perPage.

STEP 3 — Aggregate by category (the 8 names above):
- Product_Count(cat) = number of DISTINCT products whose categories array contains that category name. A product belongs to EVERY category listed in its categories array (e.g. a product with categories [Audio, Headphones] counts in both Audio and Headphones).
- Review_Count(cat) = total number of reviews across all products in that category (a product's reviews count toward every category the product belongs to).
- Avg_Rating(cat) = mean of all those review ratings, rounded to 2 decimal places.
- Five_Star_Count(cat) = count of rating==5 reviews in that category.
- Five_Star_Rate(cat) = Five_Star_Count / Review_Count * 100, rounded to 1 decimal place (0.0 if Review_Count is 0).

STEP 4 — Top Products:
Consider only products with Review_Count >= 3 (using ALL their approved reviews). Compute each product's Avg_Rating (2 dp) and Review_Count. Sort by Avg_Rating DESCENDING, then Review_Count DESCENDING, take the top 10. For each: Product_Name = product name truncated to 50 characters (Python slice name[:50], no ellipsis), Category = the name of the product's FIRST category in its categories array (the primary category), Review_Count, Avg_Rating (2 dp).

STEP 5 — Write outputs to the workspace root:
1. `products_full.json` — the complete list of all 82 products with id, name, categories.
2. `reviews_full.json` — the complete list of all 396 reviews with id, product_id, rating.
3. `analysis_data.json` — with keys:
   - "category_analysis": list of 8 dicts, each {category, product_count, review_count, avg_rating, five_star_count, five_star_rate}, one per category.
   - "top_products": list of 10 dicts, each {product_name, category, review_count, avg_rating}.
   - "email_summary": a dict with the highest-rated category (name + avg_rating) and lowest-rated category (name + avg_rating) based on Avg_Rating (ties broken by higher Review_Count for highest; for lowest pick the lower Avg_Rating, tie-break by Review_Count ascending... actually for reporting just pick one deterministically and note both).

STEP 6 — Build the Excel file Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace root using the mcp__excel__* tools:
- Sheet 1 named exactly "Category Analysis" with header row: Category, Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating, Five_Star_Count, Five_Star_Rate. One row per category, SORTED BY Category alphabetically (ascending, e.g. ... "TV & Home Theater" sorts under T). Numbers must be written as numeric values (Avg_Rating rounded 2dp, Five_Star_Rate rounded 1dp).
- Sheet 2 named exactly "Top Products" with header row: Product_Name, Category, Review_Count, Avg_Rating. The 10 rows sorted as in STEP 4.
- The default sheet created by create_workbook should be renamed/removed so the workbook has exactly these two sheets (delete any default "Sheet1" or rename it to "Category Analysis").
- Use write_data_to_excel to write values.

VERIFICATION (do all of these before finishing):
- Re-read analysis_data.json and print the full category_analysis table and top_products table.
- Sanity checks: 82 distinct products total; 396 reviews total; sum over categories of review counts > 396 (due to multi-category products); product counts per category: Audio=15, Cameras=10, Electronics=30, Headphones=10, Home Appliances=8, Speakers=5, TV & Home Theater=13, Watches=6 (these are the expected values from the category list — verify your computed values match).
- Read back the Excel file with mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata and mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel for both sheets to confirm sheets, headers, row counts, and values.

RETURN in your final message (this is the versioned deliverable contract):
1. The full 8-row category_analysis table (all fields).
2. The full 10-row top_products table (all fields).
3. The email_summary (highest/lowest category with avg ratings).
4. Confirmation that analysis_data.json and Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx were written to the workspace root, with the exact absolute paths.
5. Any anomalies (e.g. products whose category names don't exactly match the 8 canonical names).
